title: STATIC — Game Save State
description: Single source of truth for all persisted game state. Every module (economy, heat, mentors, hacking, sabotage, story) reads and writes to this shape only. No module should invent its own parallel state.

player.description: The protagonist. Single playable character (see Skill-by-Relationship design).

flags.description: Freeform boolean/string story flags, keyed by event id. e.g. 'met_deja': true, 'nova_channel_seen': true. This is how branching narrative state is tracked without a rigid quest system.

heat.description: Unified risk/exposure meter. Global, not per-mission. See Heat System module for rules on gain/decay/thresholds.

threshold_tier.description: Derived from current value by the Heat module, but cached here so other modules (economy, dialogue, mentor availability) can read it cheaply without recalculating.

history.description: Optional lightweight log of major heat events, capped at last N for debugging/narrative callbacks (e.g. a mentor referencing 'that thing you did at the data center').

lastDecayDay.description: CHANGED in 0.3.0 (was 'lastDecayAt', an ISO timestamp). Heat decays against world.day, never wall-clock time — closing the tab for a week must not decay Heat, because the fiction didn't move. Decay is idempotent per day, so it is safe to reconcile on load.

skills.description: Skill-by-relationship unlocks. Each mentor grants exactly one capability flag plus optional tiers.

aiToolAccess.description: Gated by Milo. Not a skill so much as a permission + risk tradeoff toggle.

trustedMode.description: If true, player has earned the discipline to use AI shortcuts without Milo's disapproval affecting trust. Purely narrative/dialogue gate, not a power gate.

resistanceIntel.description: Bishop's unlock. Narratively double-edged — becomes the betrayal vector in Act 2/3.

compromised.description: Flipped true at the betrayal story beat. Downstream modules (dialogue, mission availability) should check this.

relationships.description: Trust score per named NPC, independent of skill-unlock state (you can know someone without having earned their skill yet). Drives dialogue variants and mission availability.

economy.description: Black market + crypto system state. See Economy module for full pricing rules.

cryptoWallets.description: Player's own holdings, separate from stolen/drained villain wallets.

inventory.description: Owned goods (burner hardware, forged IDs, safehouse upgrades, etc.)

acquiredVia.description: Tracked for narrative flavor — e.g. stolen goods might carry Heat differently than purchased ones.

marketState.description: Price snapshot plus the live event list. Prices are DERIVED (see systems/market.ts priceOf) and cached here the way heat.threshold_tier is, so a save file is readable on its own; nothing should read them to make a decision.

activeEvents.description: CHANGED in 0.5.0 (was string[]). A bare id could record that an event had started but never that it had finished, so a crackdown raised gear prices permanently. The multiplier table stays in economy content; only the instance lives here. `scope` is on the instance because one definition can fire against different categories depending on what triggered it.

villainWallets.description: ADDED in 0.5.0 (SCHEMA-NOTES gap 3). Villain wallets existed only once drained, but the recon phase's entire output is DISCOVERING one, and a failed heist hardens it — both before any drain. Balance and security tier are copied in from mission content on discovery, because they change afterwards and the content object must not.

balance.description: Narrative-scaled. Zeroed on a drain rather than deleted — the player found it, and that stays true.

clues.description: Recon clue ids gathered. Which heist methods are open is derived from these.

villainWalletsDrained.description: Tracks which named villain wallets have been hit, for story-gating (can't drain twice, unlocks reactions/escalation).

redistributed.description: Portion sent back out via Robin Hood mechanic vs kept for resistance funding.

activeConsumables.description: ADDED in 0.5.0 (SCHEMA-NOTES gap 6). clean_sim is spec'd as lasting 'for that session'; there is no session in this schema and there shouldn't be, so it lasts until the next in-fiction day, which world.day makes expressible.

expiresOnDay.description: Exclusive, same convention as a market event.

missions.description: ADDED in 0.2.0. Structured per-mission state, keyed by mission id. This is the home for anything repeatable and shaped: retry cooldowns, target hardening, banked partial progress, and the four-beat mentor template's current beat. player.flags stays for genuine one-off branching, which is what it is good at.

beat.description: Mentor missions only: the four-beat template's cursor, and what closes the door behind a mentor scene the way a chapter advance does for act content. 1-4 are the template's beats; higher numbers are branch beats (Files' recovery path runs to 6); 0 is the sentinel meaning the mission is finished, which is deliberately a value no scene gates on.

hardened.description: Raised by a failed run. Tightens the Trace Counter / Alertness budget on retry. It does NOT regenerate the map — a hardened target is the same building with tighter security, which is what keeps bankedIntel valid.

cooldownUntilDay.description: world.day the mission becomes attemptable again.

bankedIntel.description: Trace: node indices already revealed, carried into the retry.

prepped.description: ADDED in 0.3.0. A hacking trace has been run against this target, which reveals the hidden casing detail on the sabotage side (Sabotage module, Tier 4 cross-skill hook).

world.description: Town-state effects, mostly ambient/systemic rather than player-inventory.

townTrust.description: Ambient town-wide sentiment, shifted by Robin Hood payouts and public sabotage outcomes. Drives background flavor (NPC dialogue, environmental storytelling) rather than hard gates.

burnedOnDay.description: ADDED in 0.6.0. When it was burned, so it can recover on its own after a few days rather than being lost — nothing in this game is permanently taken away from the player. Measured against world.day.

day.description: ADDED in 0.2.0. The single in-fiction clock. Heat decay, mission cooldowns and (Phase 5) market event expiry all read this. Advanced by explicit story/rest actions, never by real time.

settings.description: Non-narrative player prefs. Doesn't affect other modules.

reducedFlicker.description: ADDED in 0.2.0. In-game control over the glitch effect's flicker, chromatic aberration and palette invert. Defaults from the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting, but is changeable in-game because a player on a shared machine cannot change an OS setting.

cross_module_rules: Heat.threshold_tier is READ by: economy (price volatility + vendor willingness), skills.resistanceIntel (Bishop's availability), mentor missions (some become locked at 'hunted'), and both minigames (a smaller budget). Every one of those nudges must be VISIBLE to the player — the meter renders a shorter bar, it does not quietly change a denominator.
world.day is the only clock. heat.lastDecayDay, missions.*.cooldownUntilDay and economy market events all measure against it. Nothing in the save may decay or expire against wall-clock time.
relationships.trust is the gate for skills.*.unlocked transitions — a mentor mission's completion writes both a relationships.trust delta AND flips skills.<x>.unlocked.
economy.villainWalletsDrained entries should trigger heat.history events and world.townTrust deltas — theft isn't free narratively even when it's a 'win'.
skills.resistanceIntel.compromised = true is the single flag that flips Act 2→3 — all modules should check this before showing 'trust the resistance' dialogue/mission options.
No module writes directly to another module's subtree except through these documented cross-effects — keeps modules independently testable.
STILL OPEN (see SCHEMA-NOTES.md): economy.villainWallets (gap 3) and a structured economy.marketState.activeEvents (gap 4) are both required before Phase 5 and are deliberately not invented here.

economy.marketState.activeEvents and economy.activeConsumables both expire against world.day. Anything that advances the day must age them (systems/market.ts tickMarket) — an event that cannot expire is a price change that never ends.

A drain writes FOUR things together: economy.cashOnHand, economy.villainWalletsDrained, a heat.history entry and a world.townTrust delta. They live in one function (systems/heist.ts drain) because splitting them across call sites is how one gets forgotten.

world.safehouses is written by content (the `safehouse` effect) and read by market.ts, which will not sell a safehouse-category good until one exists and installs it there rather than into economy.inventory — you cannot carry a power rig around.
